name: tma_store_loaded
findings_from_v1: see protocol.json addendum 2026-11-10: the store-epilogue round costs 575-600 cycles per 8 KiB on one SM alone (independent of the number of SMs), the sim's round is ~125 cycles + ring drain; the stretch is cluster-local and made of a fence step, a UTMASTG + commit hold and the barrier waits; the store map geometry changes the store time; loads in flight on the same SM lengthen the fence step.
question: For one SM: (1) how long do UTMASTG + UTMACMDFLUSH hold the issuing warp, and when does the bulk group complete, as a function of the box bytes and of the store map geometry (row bytes, swizzle, L2 promotion, global row stride); (2) how long does the smem-write + fence.proxy.async step take per warp as a function of the bytes the warps wrote, of a TMA store in flight and of TMA loads in flight; (3) which warps are held, and until when, while thread 0 issues the store; (4) does the full round equal the composition of (1)-(3); (5) is any of it different when all SMs run it.
probe: tools/microbench/tma_store_loaded/probe/store_round.cu (header comment = the round shapes). MODE full / fence / store / sts, STAGES 1 or 4, STAMPS 0 or 1. STAMPS 1 accumulates in registers the absolute clock64 of six stamps (A round start, B after the fence step, C after barrier 1, D after UTMASTG + commit, E after wait_group, F after barrier 2) for lane 0 of each of the four epilogue warps; the host reports per-warp mean offsets from warp 0's A, so the relative timing of the four warps is measured (v1 had two threads and only differences). Store map: 16-bit elements, box = row_bytes x (box_bytes / row_bytes) rows, geometry G64W = 64 B rows, SWIZZLE_64B, promotion 128B, global stride 10496 B (the captured CUF-DSL store map); G64 the same with stride 64; G64N promotion none; G128 = 128 B rows, SWIZZLE_128B, promotion 128B (the tma_forms / nvjet / FIF map); G128N promotion none; G128P promotion 256B (the DGF maps); G256N = 256 B rows, no swizzle, promotion none (v1). Destination ring of 4 boxes per CTA, written once by cudaMemset at start. Loaders: 4 x 16 KiB UTMALDG slots, each CTA cycling over its own 64 boxes after two untimed read-warm launches. 264 rounds, first 8 not counted, 8 repetitions after a discarded one, runs a and b.
cells: run.sh with V2=1 (78 cells per run): controls; store-only: 7 geometries x STAGES {1,4} x STAMPS {0,1} at 8 KiB, box 2 / 16 KiB on G64W (STAGES 1, 4) and G128 (STAGES 4), G64W with 4 loaders at N in {1, NMAX}, G64W at NMAX; fence-only: writers in {0,1,4} and writers {0,4} with 4 loaders; full round: G64W and G128 x N in {1, NMAX} x L in {0,4}, G256N, G64W STAGES 1, G64W writers 1; each STAMPS 0 and 1.
sass_gate: sass_check_v2.py (run by build_v2.sh, failure stops the run): 16 k_round instantiations with the per-mode counts in its docstring.
derivation: model_v2.py. From warp 0's timeline: fence = B - A, bar1 = C - B, hold = D - C, wait = E - D, bar2 = F - E; completion = E - C at STAGES 1 (issue start to wait_group 0 return); period from STAMPS 0. Per-warp offsets of A, B, C, F from warp 0's A.
acceptance: Controls, nothing else is read if one fails: (C1) store-only G128 STAGES 1: completion at 2 / 8 / 16 KiB within 20 % of the installed storage.tma.completion UTMASTG tile values (b300 76 / 275 / 524, h100 126 / 322 / 574); (C2) loader-only N = 1: within 15 % of tma_loaded N1.S4 (b300 92.7, h100 88.9 B/cycle). Runs a / b within 5 % per cell. A STAMPS 1 timeline is used only if its period is within 15 % of the STAMPS 0 period of the same cell; where it is not, only the STAMPS 0 period of that cell is used.

rule_forms_declared_before_data.S1_hold: hold(box bytes, geometry) from store-only STAGES 4 (ring not full). Form: the warp that issued UTMASTG is held from the UTMASTG issue until hold cycles later (engine: the warp's next-issue floor, the way MEMBAR / FENCE results already set control_floor). Accepted if hold is the same (within 10 %) in store-only and full rounds of the same geometry and is described within 10 % at 2 / 8 / 16 KiB by a + bytes / rate. Leaf: instruction.service UTMASTG result latency cannot carry a byte axis today; the hold goes into storage.async.service_start UTMASTG tile (the field the tree already has per transfer_bytes: b300 64 / 256 / 512 at 2 / 8 / 16 KiB) if the measured hold on G128 reproduces that field within 15 % (then the rule only adds its use as the issuer's hold, no value changes); otherwise a new field hold_cycles on storage.tma.completion UTMASTG with the measured knots.
rule_forms_declared_before_data.S2_completion_geometry: completion(8 KiB, geometry) over the 7 geometries. Candidate single measures, fixed here: raw box bytes (no geometry dependence, all within 10 %); promoted bytes = rows x (row span rounded up to the L2 promotion granularity; none = 32 B sectors); row count; sector count. The measure is accepted if completion = a + b x measure fits all 7 geometries and the G64W box scan within 10 % with one (a, b); then storage.tma.completion UTMASTG gets that measure as its axis (a converter-derived fact of the captured tensor map) with the measured knots. If none fits: recorded, no install, the existing bytes leaf stays.
rule_forms_declared_before_data.S3_fence: fence step per warp from fence-only rounds: writers 0 (nothing written) vs 1 vs 4. Forms: (i) constant per warp (all warps' B offsets equal within 15 cycles, independent of writers): instruction.service FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S / MEMBAR.ALL.CTA result latency re-measured here replaces the installed 9 + 9 only through a service_latency addendum; (ii) per-SM serial: the warps' B offsets are staggered and the last B grows with the bytes written: one per-SM server, cost per fencing warp = stagger, charged in arrival order; (iii) waits for the SM's async engine: the fence step in full rounds / with loaders exceeds the fence-only step by the time the previous store (resp. the loads) still occupy the engine: fence completion >= the engine's busy-until. Whichever of (i)-(iii) the fence-only, full and loader cells select (each must hold on both runs and reproduce the full-round fence step within 15 %) is the declared engine rule; a mixture or none: recorded, v3.
rule_forms_declared_before_data.S4_held_warps: from the four-warp timelines of full rounds: if the non-issuing warps leave barrier 1 (C) later than warp 0 by more than 30 cycles, the hold of S1 applies to every warp of the CTA that passed the barrier (CTA-wide hold until the UTMASTG hold ends); else only the issuer is held.
rule_forms_declared_before_data.S5_composition: full-round period (STAMPS 0) predicted = fence step (S3) + cta.release + hold (S1) + cta.release + ring wait (STAGES 4: 0 unless completion > 3 periods); accepted if within 15 % of the measured period for G64W, G128 and G256N at N = 1, L = 0; the L = 4 and NMAX cells are then predictions to check (within 20 %), not fits.
rule_forms_declared_before_data.S6_full_gpu: if a G64W full or store-only period at NMAX exceeds its N = 1 period by more than 15 % the excess is gpu-shared and is recorded for a separate protocol; cluster-local rules above are installed from N = 1 cells only.

install: a rule is installed only in its declared form with values from the named cells, evidence measured when runs a / b agree within 5 %; source tma_store_loaded.<device>.<run> (artifact $A/microbench/tma_store_loaded/<device>-<run>/, model $A/fg-gemm/tsl/<device>-v2-model.json). The leaves are cluster-local: gate = single-cluster 500 x 2 against $A/fg-fix5/sc-r7 (MAPE must not get worse) and full-gpu 500 x 2 against $A/fg-fix5/full-r7, CTest, pytest, cyclescope tree validate --strict.
not_allowed: no case-cycle tuning; no values from other machines; no threshold, form or derivation change after data; one device's leaf is not copied to the other.

addenda.text: Control C1 failed in its absolute form (see protocol-v3.json findings_from_v2); no rule of v2 is evaluated, nothing installed. Superseded by protocol-v3.json.

addenda.after_run: r3 binaries, new collections fg-gemm/epilogue-replay/hw-extra-{b300,h100} and engine replay fg-gemm/epilogue-replay/base-{b300,h100}
addenda.text: Written after seeing data; v2's control C1 stays failed and none of its declared rule forms is claimed. Reason for reopening: per-PC attribution of CUF-DSL-BS-NVF4-V16-R05 (fg-gemm/jr10) puts 126 k of 169 k hardware warp-cycles per CTA on the epilogue fence / barrier PCs against 24 k simulated. Engine replay of 17 store_round cells per device (frozen r3 binary, traced launch, build 1425790c): STAMPS 0 periods simulated / hardware b300 | h100: sts writers 4 253.5 / 262.3 | 253.9 / 262.3, store-only 254.5 / 257.0 | 258.8 / 257.1, fence writers 0 91.6 / 95.8 | 74.6 / 94.0 agree; fence writers 1 91.6 / 213.0 | 91.6 / 211.0, fence writers 4 253.9 / 354.0 | 254.2 / 349.0 and the full round 316.1 / 412.8 | 345.8 / 411.9 do not: the engine completes a fence 9 cycles after issue, in parallel with the acceptance of the stores it follows. New hardware cells (same binary, no tracer, two runs identical to 0.3 cycle, GPU-c7323916 and GPU-fcfb3306): STAMPS 0 periods for writers 0..4, sts 66.8 / 132.6 / 141.1 / 203.7 / 262.3 and fence 95.8 / 213.0 / 222.5 / 287.3 / 354.0 on b300, sts 65.3 / 131.3 / 141.1 / 203.8 / 262.3 and fence 94.0 / 211.0 / 217.5 / 286.3 / 349.0 on h100. Derivation fixed here: D(W) = fence(W) - sts(W) is the time a fence after W x 2048 written bytes adds to the round; W = 0 gives the clean fence (29.0 | 28.75); ordinary least squares of D over written bytes for W = 1..4 gives D = 75.26 + bytes / 569.0 (b300, residuals at most 2.6 cycles) and 74.51 + bytes / 751.8 (h100, at most 3.6). Rule: a proxy fence issued while its CTA has synchronous shared stores accepted since its previous fence completes at max(issue, end of their acceptance) + cycles + bytes / drain_bytes_per_cycle and holds the issuing warp until then; a fence with nothing written keeps its service latency. Evidence experimental (post-data form, one geometry: 64 B per thread, one CTA per SM). Check: replay of the same captured cells must bring fence writers 4 and the full round within 5 percent of the hardware STAMPS 0 period and leave sts, store-only and fence writers 0 unchanged. Not covered and recorded: with four TMA load slots in flight D is 171 (writers 1) and 182 (writers 4) on b300 while the clean fence is unchanged, i.e. loads in flight about double the dirty fence; the engine also hides a single writer warp's store cost (fence writers 1 stays near 170 against 213). STAMPS 1 timelines show the fence instruction returning early and the following bar.sync leaving about 100 cycles later (22 when clean); the rule charges the wait at the fence, which is equivalent for fence-then-barrier epilogues.
